description:
Problem: the local review requires the omp on PATH to equal the CI pin (_project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/local.py check_harness), but the build URL and SHA-256 are pinned only for linux-x64, inside .github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml. The owner's Mac runs the Tern-managed omp 18.12.6, so on 2026-10-26 every review-required make pr-open refused (8 refusals). Seven agent runs side-loaded an unverified darwin-arm64 18.12.1 build into ~/.cache/omp-18.12.1/bin (SHA-256 fa41b27d434380e99b713e4f9ced0f73eb1fc0c409fdf23a57c119971d24bac5, provenance unchecked) and one bypassed make pr-open with gh pr create (#3537). Cloud bootstrap reads the URL and SHA from the branch's workflow while the local review reads the version from origin/develop, so a stale branch installs a build the review then refuses; non-linux-x64 cloud images get no omp at all.

Outcome: one pinned config (gate 4) holds the version and, per platform, the URL and SHA-256 (linux-x64 and darwin-arm64 at least; linux-arm64 if the build host publishes it). CI's install step, scripts/cloud_gateway.sh and the local review all read it; local and cloud read it from origin/develop. One verified installer downloads the platform build into a versioned cache (for example ~/.cache/benchbox/omp/<version>/<platform>/omp), checks SHA-256 before marking it executable, and the review invokes that binary by path, never the omp on PATH. The installer is part of the self-contained reviewer package (owner Q11: split-ready).

Decision gates:
1. SHA provenance (darwin-arm64 resolved 2026-10-26: the official build at https://build.stencil.so/d/omp/20261017-231446-291e055/omp-darwin-arm64, downloaded over TLS, has SHA-256 fa41b27d434380e99b713e4f9ced0f73eb1fc0c409fdf23a57c119971d24bac5, is byte-identical to the side-loaded cache binary and reports omp/18.12.1). Use a checksum the build host publishes if one exists; otherwise compute it from a TLS download, record the method in the PR body and in docs/internal/oracle-review-v2.md, and match how the existing linux-x64 pin was established (git log -S on the SHA). Compare against the side-loaded binary's SHA above and record match or mismatch. Stop and ask if the darwin artifact does not report exactly the pinned version.
2. Platform coverage. A platform without a pinned artifact makes the review unable to run (owner decision #8: refuse), with a message naming the platform; never fall back to PATH omp.
3. CI equivalence. The CI install step must install the same linux-x64 URL, SHA and version as today, now read from the pin file; prove it with a workflow test.
4. Pin location: extend an existing pinned config (.github/oracle-omp-config.yml or .github/oracle-reviewers.yml) so the reviewer keeps one pinned config (owner Q11); a new file needs a recorded reason.

Until oracle-gateway-cloud-builder-access-20261025 merges, publish only from the owner's Mac.
